lineage: Beauregard PID (2011-): a widely-copied, carefully-engineered PID controller -- proportional/integral/derivative feedback with anti-windup, derivative-on-measurement, and bumpless mode switching; the reference small feedback controller of the maker world
version: github.com/br3ttb/Arduino-PID-Library master as of 2026-09-12 (commit in hashes)
build_system: compile PID_v1.cpp with a Techne Arduino-shim + a plant simulator
dependencies: an Arduino.h shim providing millis() (Techne harness supplies a minimal one)
entry_points: PID::Compute() -- run each control step on (Input, Setpoint) -> Output

example.command: Techne harness: a first-order plant + PID, step the setpoint, log the response
example.output: the controlled variable converging to setpoint

upstream_docs: Beauregard, Improving the Beginner's PID (blog series)

human_capability_summary.built_to: drive a measured process variable to a setpoint by feeding back the error through proportional, integral and derivative terms, robustly, on a tiny microcontroller
human_capability_summary.pressure: actuator limits (windup), noisy measurements (derivative kick), and mode changes (bumpless transfer) in a real physical loop with lag
human_capability_summary.success_means: the process variable reaches and holds the setpoint with acceptable overshoot/settling despite disturbances and saturation

known_human_problem_solved: closed-loop regulation of a physical process
human_environmental_pressure: actuator lag and saturation, measurement noise, load disturbance, setpoint changes
human_failure_condition: oscillation or runaway: bad gains make the loop unstable; integral windup overshoots; the controlled machine overheats/crashes/breaks
behavioral_entry_point: change the setpoint (step), inject a load disturbance, or set aggressive gains (Kp/Ki high) to drive it UNSTABLE -- the harness does the last as a pathological-behavior receipt

nyx_handoff.how_to_run_it: recipe.json (runner docker); python -m techne.fossils.harvest run arduino-pid
nyx_handoff.what_humans_used_it_for: drive a measured process variable to a setpoint by feeding back the error through proportional, integral and derivative terms, robustly, on a tiny microcontroller
